name: General science
description: States of matter, atoms, forces, energy, cells and ecosystems.

skills.name: States of matter
skills.rubric: Describes solids, liquids and gases and changes of state using particles

skills.name: Atoms and elements
skills.rubric: Identifies atoms, elements, compounds and subatomic particles

skills.name: Forces and motion
skills.rubric: Names forces, calculates speed and applies balanced-force reasoning

skills.name: Energy
skills.rubric: Identifies energy stores, transfers and conservation

skills.name: Cells
skills.rubric: Identifies cell parts and their functions in plants and animals

skills.name: Ecosystems
skills.rubric: Interprets food chains and explains changes in populations

items.prompt: Which state of matter keeps a fixed shape?
items.hint: Think of an ice cube compared with water or steam.

items.prompt: What is it called when a liquid turns into a gas?
items.hint: Puddles do this on a sunny day.

items.prompt: At what temperature does pure water boil at sea level?
items.hint: Water freezes at 0 °C and boils at a round number.

items.prompt: In which state are the particles furthest apart?
options: They are always the same distance apart
items.hint: This state can be squashed most easily.

items.prompt: What is it called when a solid turns straight into a gas?
items.hint: Dry ice does this.

items.prompt: Why does a gas spread out to fill its whole container?
options: Its particles are held in fixed positions
Its particles move freely in all directions
items.hint: Think about how the particles move.

items.prompt: What is the smallest particle of an element?
items.hint: Everything is built from these.

items.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
items.hint: It is a single capital letter.

items.prompt: Which particle in an atom has a negative charge?
items.hint: These particles move around the nucleus.

items.prompt: What is the chemical formula for water?
items.hint: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

items.prompt: An atom has 6 protons. What is its atomic number?
items.hint: The atomic number is the number of protons.

items.prompt: Which of these is a compound?
items.hint: A compound contains more than one element joined together.

items.prompt: Which force pulls objects towards the Earth?
items.hint: It is why things fall.

items.prompt: What is the unit of force?
items.hint: It is named after a famous scientist.

items.prompt: A car travels 100 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
items.hint: Speed is distance divided by time.

items.prompt: Which force slows down an object sliding across a table?
items.hint: It acts between surfaces that rub together.

items.prompt: The forces on a moving object are balanced. What happens to its motion?
options: It keeps the same speed and direction
items.hint: Only unbalanced forces change motion.

items.prompt: A force of 10 N acts on a mass of 2 kg. What is the acceleration?
items.hint: Acceleration is force divided by mass.

items.prompt: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
items.hint: It will not run out.

items.prompt: What kind of energy does a moving object have?
items.hint: The faster it moves, the more it has.

items.prompt: What is the unit of energy?
items.hint: Food labels often use thousands of these.

items.prompt: Which energy transfer happens in a battery-powered torch?
items.hint: Start with what is stored in the battery.

items.prompt: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred. What is this law called?
items.hint: 'Conserved' means the total stays the same.

items.prompt: A ball is lifted higher above the ground. Which energy store increases?
items.hint: It depends on height.

items.prompt: What is the basic building block of all living things?
items.hint: Your body has trillions of them.

items.prompt: Which part of a cell controls its activities?
items.hint: It contains the genetic material.

items.prompt: Which part is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
items.hint: It gives plant cells a rigid shape.

items.prompt: Where does photosynthesis take place in a plant cell?
items.hint: These parts are green.

items.prompt: What is the main job of mitochondria?
items.hint: They are often called the powerhouses of the cell.

items.prompt: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
items.hint: Plants give out oxygen and take in this gas.

items.prompt: What do we call an animal that eats only plants?
items.hint: Cows and rabbits are examples.

items.prompt: Where does almost all the energy in a food chain come from originally?
items.hint: Plants capture it with their leaves.

items.prompt: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, what is the rabbit?
items.hint: It is the first animal to eat in the chain.

items.prompt: What do decomposers such as fungi do?
items.hint: They recycle nutrients back into the soil.

items.prompt: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, all the foxes disappear. What is most likely to happen first?
items.hint: Think about what was eating the rabbits.

items.prompt: Why are there usually fewer predators than prey in an ecosystem?
options: Energy is lost at each step of the food chain
items.hint: Less energy is available higher up the chain.
